transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-18 16:00 PDT | Duration 62m | Attendees: Jordan Park, Samir Patel (Redwood); Maya Thompson (CISO), Rajesh Iyer (Head of SRE), Ellen Brooks (Security Eng), Tom Alvarez (PO)

[00:00] Jordan Park: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, there's a lot to go through so we'll try to be crisp. job is to understand the pentest results and align on remediation and patch cadence.
[00:14] Maya Thompson: great, thanks jordan. quick context — pen test was done by RedFox in late May, scope included our VPC-hosted services and the web gateway. we got the executive summary last week.
[00:28] Ellen Brooks: i'll flag up front, the report has three criticals, seven high, and a number of mediums, some false positives too. there's an appendix with poc screenshots but it's messy.
[00:42] Samir Patel: can you clarify the criticals — remote code exec? auth bypass? just to frame remediation effort.
[00:50] Ellen Brooks: two are auth bypasses in an admin API (missing token check under a specific header flow), one is privilege escalation via a container image with outdated libs — openssl, libc. CVSSs are 9.1, 8.8, 9.0-ish, so high risk.
[01:06] Rajesh Iyer: the container one maps to a base image we inherited from an old pipeline, it's used in staging and a subset of prod jobs. we're already isolating those workloads.
[01:18] Tom Alvarez: and we have a compliance window for EU patient data, so any prod fixes need to be in-line with our data residency and deployment freeze windows — just flagging timeline constraints.
[01:30] Jordan Park: understood. quick Q on process — how are you triaging? jira, slack channel, who owns criticals?
[01:36] Ellen Brooks: jira, but it's mixed with day-to-day. i'm proposing an EPIC called "pentest-may-2025" and create sub-tasks by severity. criticals get 72-hour SLA to mitigation or an approved risk acceptance.
[01:50] Samir Patel: that's good. for Redwood private customers we normally see a pattern: immediate mitigation for criticals, temporary mitigation (WAF rules, rate limits) while full patch lands. are you comfortable with those compensating controls?
[02:04] Maya Thompson: yes but we need to document them for SOC 2 evidence — which is why audit logs and change records are critical.
[02:12] Jordan Park: on that note, Redwood can provide a change-log export and immutable audit log samples from private deployments; samir will share the export template after the call.
[02:24] Ellen Brooks: perfect. also curious about KMS options — we use cloud-KMS in EU region, rotation policy is every 90 days. any recommendations?
[02:34] Samir Patel: rotation every 90 days is okay, we recommend automated rotation tied to HSM/KMS where possible, with key versioning so you can roll back. Redwood supports both customer-managed keys (BYOK) and our managed CMKs. for SOC 2 you probably want customer-managed + rotation proof.
[02:52] Rajesh Iyer: can you show the KMS integration? are there changes to latency or availability if we go BYOK?
[02:58] Samir Patel: small impact on cold-starts for key operations, but negligible in steady-state — we'll send benchmark numbers.
[03:06] Tom Alvarez: back to patching cadence — we've historically been monthly with emergency patches for critical CVEs. pen-test seems to suggest we need to tighten that. any best practices?
[03:18] Jordan Park: many customers run monthly regular updates and a weekly advisory check for new criticals. Redwood's notification hooks can create issues in your tracker when a model/runtime dependency hits a CVE threshold.
[03:32] Ellen Brooks: do you integrate with SCA tooling? we run Snyk and OSS-Fuzz in our pipeline but coverage isn't perfect.
[03:40] Samir Patel: we don't ship an SCA, but we integrate with artifact metadata and can ingest SBOMs. recommended pattern: SCA during CI (fail build for critical), dependency pinning, and weekly dependency scans in production.
[03:54] Maya Thompson: secure SDLC — are you recommending pre-commit SCA or shift-left runtime checks? we need evidence for iso27001 as well.
[04:04] Samir Patel: both; shift-left prevents regressions, runtime checks catch drift. also run fuzzing and scheduled dependency sweeps. Redwood can provide signing and container image attestations as evidence.
[04:18] Ellen Brooks: about the auth bypass, our initial mitigation is adding header checks and rate limits, but we're worried about stale tokens and RBAC misconfig. any config advice?
[04:30] Samir Patel: ensure token validation is central (not multiple custom checks) and adopt RBAC roles tied to least privilege. Redwood RBAC supports scoped tokens for routes and service accounts; we'll share sample policies.
[04:44] Rajesh Iyer: for private deployment, how do you surface audit logs and what retention options exist? we need 2 years for SOC 2 type II evidence.
[04:53] Jordan Park: audit logs are configurable — events, tokens, admin actions. retention can be extended; many customers ship logs to their SIEM (Splunk, Sumo Logic). we can also provide offsite archive exports for the retention window.
[05:06] Ellen Brooks: does Redwood sign logs or provide tamper-evidence?
[05:10] Samir Patel: we support log immutability options and export to append-only storage; signing can be arranged through KMS-based attestations.
[05:20] Tom Alvarez: re: remediation SLAs — do you have examples of remediation tracking dashboards or runbooks?
[05:27] Jordan Park: yes, Redwood Console has per-route and per-model dashboards; for security events you can create incident playbooks and link to runbooks. we'll share a sample runbook for container patching.
[05:40] Ellen Brooks: for the container CVE, are you recommending rebuilds and redeploys only, or live patching?
[05:46] Samir Patel: rebuild + redeploy is preferred. live patching is risky and incomplete. apply compensating WAF rules until redeploy.
[05:58] Rajesh Iyer: ok. who's doing retest? the pen-test vendor offers a quick retest fee — do we recommend retest after fixes or after full regression?
[06:08] Jordan Park: retest after fixes and evidence is uploaded; often a targeted retest for criticals within 2 weeks.
[06:14] Maya Thompson: budget constraints are a concern, but criticals need fast closure.
[06:18] Ellen Brooks: i'll prioritize the two auth bypass issues and the container vuln as critical; create tickets tonight.
[06:24] Samir Patel: quick note on data residency: if you run private stacks in EU, encryption-at-rest + tenant isolation + KMS in-region satisfies many regulators, but you must verify backups' locations.
[06:37] Tom Alvarez: backups currently replicate to a secondary eu-west-3 region; needed to confirm that meets our residency policy.
[06:44] Jordan Park: we'll add a short checklist for backup residency and proof artifacts.
[06:50] Ellen Brooks: on SSO — we've got Okta, SAML v2.0; any gotchas for private deployments?
[06:56] Samir Patel: ensure assertion mapping to RBAC roles is consistent; test session expiry behavior and SSO fallback. also enforce MFA for admin roles.
[07:08] Rajesh Iyer: timeline and recaps — we aim to close criticals in 72 hours, highs in 14 days, medium in 30 days. is that reasonable?
[07:18] Jordan Park: reasonable. for retest, schedule a 2-week follow-up to verify progress, with a 30-day full remediation snapshot for SOC evidence.
[07:25] Maya Thompson: ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[07:30] Jordan Park: recap: Ellen uploads full report and artifacts; Jordan shares whitepaper and audit-log template; Samir shares patch cadence recommendations and KMS integration notes; Rajesh creates the Jira EPIC and assigns owners. schedule follow-up in two weeks for re-test check-in.
[07:50] Ellen Brooks: i'll do the uploads today and assign owners. thanks.
[07:56] Tom Alvarez: thanks everyone.
[08:00] Jordan Park: we'll circulate notes and have the next call on 2025-07-02 if that works — two weeks out. thanks all.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-transcriptions of product names (Redwood referred to as "red wood"), some acronyms flagged incorrectly (KV cache -> K V cache). the speakers used filler words and there was a short dropped packet at 00:53 leading to a partial sentence.
